name: Rukbat
description: A star 56 parsecs away, 2.5 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.

radius.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95347: radius 2.472 solar radii, implied by the fitted luminosity 122.118 solar luminosities (fractional uncertainty 0.431) and temperature

temperature.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95347: effective temperature 12212 +/- 3038 K, from the fit of a model atmosphere to the star's spectral energy distribution (goodness of fit Q 0.02)

distance.source: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770, table 2, HIP 95347: distance 55.741 pc, the paper's parallax inverted (Gaia DR1's where it revised the star's, else the Hipparcos reduction of van Leeuwen 2007; section 2.3; fractional uncertainty 0.012), at which the luminosity and radius hold

limb.none: no mass is measured and no spectroscopic surface gravity is published with this radius: McDonald, Zijlstra & Watson (2017), MNRAS 471, 770 assume the gravity of their fit (table column 15)

text.card: A star 56 parsecs away, 2.5 times the Sun's width, measured from its light.
text.introduction: Its brightness, measured band by band, gives 122 times the Sun's luminosity at 12,212 K, so 2.472 solar radii.
text.locator: Table 2, HIP 95347: D, Teff, L, Rad, Q

quotes.title: Alpha Sagittarii
quotes.card: Alpha Sagittarii, also named Rukbat, is a star in the constellation of Sagittarius.

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 6713727061309245952 (quality C), from 2006AstL...32..759G; Gaia DR3 measures none
